methodology: causal

# Diagnosing why breaches happen

Pulling the thread on the last twenty breach events against the logger data turned up a more specific cause than "insulation runs out eventually." Every one of the twenty events happened on a route where the fourth stop or later fell during the two hours around midday, the hottest part of the day and also the point where the van's rear doors had already been opened and closed, cumulatively, the most times.

That points at door-open duration and frequency as the actual driver, not total route length by itself; a six-stop route completed entirely in the cooler morning hours shows almost no breach risk in the same data. The team has not yet tested whether resequencing routes to front-load midday stops earlier, or simply shielding the door zone better, would matter more, and there is a live disagreement between the two ideas that nobody has settled with data yet, only with opinion, which is itself worth naming since opinion is exactly what got this problem overlooked the first time around.
